newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt urges quick end to peace crisis.
newsitem.headline: Egypt urges quick end to peace crisis.

text.p: Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak said on Tuesday he feared the present crisis in the Middle East peace process could lead to more violence if it is not resolved quickly.
Mubarak also told reporters after talks with Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy that it was "dangerous" to weaken Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's position.

Asked if he had any formula to restart the peace process, Mubarak said: "At least to find the solution to the present situation now, because the present situation may help much more terrorism. This is our fear. Secondly we have to slow down the so-called settlements and these things."
Mubarak and Levy held the talks in Cairo on a crisis in the Middle East peace process heightened by suicide bombings in Jerusalem last week in which 15 people died.
Israel cracked down on Palestinian self-ruled areas after the attacks last week.
Middle Eastern leaders are criss-crossing the region in search of a way out of the crisis.

Mubarak, asked if he was worried the attacks weakened Arafat locally and in Israeli eyes, said: "Weakening the position of Arafat is very, very dangerous in the peace process. Whether somebody understands or doesn't understand it's very important to keep him in power.

"We said that punishing the Palestinians -- no food, no medicine -- is very dangerous and may have very negative reactions and I ask them to find a quick solution to the present situation in what will be next for the peace."
